links.title: Obi-otoshi on the IJF technique reference

about.en: A hand throw driven from the belt: tori takes the front of uke's belt, shifts behind uke's right side, and scoops uke's upper left leg from behind with the other hand to throw them backwards. One of the Kodokan techniques recognised beyond the Gokyo, and a useful answer to a partner who stands square and heavy.

en: Take the front of the belt with your right hand
Shift behind their right side as you pull the belt towards you
Your belt hand and your scooping hand move as one
Face your partner and take the front of their belt with your right hand; feel for the knot to place the hand.
Pull the belt towards you and, at the same moment, shift your body behind their right side.
Reach your left arm across the front of their body and scoop their left leg from behind, high on the thigh.
Lift with the scooping hand while the belt hand keeps pulling, so their balance breaks backwards.
They fall backwards and land on their back; keep hold of the belt so they land under control.

receiving.en: A hand takes the front of your belt and your partner moves behind your right side, then an arm crosses your front and scoops your left thigh from behind. Your feet lift and you go down backwards. Tuck your chin and slap with both arms as your back meets the mat.

viNotes.en: The belt is the easiest landmark on a judogi, so this is a friendly throw to find: feel for the knot at the front to place your right hand. The posture it answers, square and heavy, is also one you can read through the grips before committing. Move behind their right side without letting the belt go, and slide your left hand across their front and down to the back of their left thigh so it never leaves their body. Keep the belt as they go down so you know where they have landed.

cue.en: One hand takes the front of the belt, the other scoops the opponent's thigh from behind, and they are thrown down backwards.
